name: Pleuropulmonary Blastoma Type 3

criteria.description: Presence of a solid, high-grade malignant neoplasm composed predominantly of undifferentiated blastematous and sarcomatous cells without cystic components
Radiologic evidence of a large, solid intrathoracic mass arising from the lung or pleura without cystic lesions
Detection of DICER1 gene mutations in tumor tissue or germline DNA

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathologic confirmation of a solid pleuropulmonary blastoma tumor (type 3) with supportive imaging findings; genetic testing for DICER1 mutations is supportive but not mandatory.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Differentiation from type 1 and 2 PPB is critical; type 3 lacks cystic components and is more aggressive.

pathognomonic.notes: Typically presents as a palpable chest mass or visible thoracic asymmetry

pathognomonic.symptomName: Respiratory distress due to lung compression
searchTerms: respiratory distress due to mass effect
shortness of breath from lung pressure

common.symptomName: Chest pain localized to tumor site

occasional.symptomName: Weight loss and failure to thrive
searchTerms: failure to gain weight and lose weight
fever and weight loss from cancer
systemic symptoms like fever and fatigue

rare.symptomName: Metastatic symptoms such as bone pain
searchTerms: pain in bones due to metastasis
symptoms from cancer spread to bones

laboratory: Non-specific inflammatory markers elevation (e.g., elevated ESR, CRP)
imaging: Chest X-ray showing large solid intrathoracic mass
CT scan revealing a heterogeneous solid tumor without cystic components
MRI may show tumor extent and involvement of adjacent structures
genetic: DICER1 gene mutations detected in tumor or germline DNA
other: Histopathology demonstrating undifferentiated blastematous and sarcomatous cells
Immunohistochemistry positive for markers such as vimentin and desmin

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of cystic lung lesions rather than solid mass
Lack of malignant blastematous cells on histology
Epithelial origin tumor rather than mesenchymal blastematous tumor
Mixed cystic and solid tumor components
Histopathology shows both cystic and solid areas

redFlags: Large thoracic mass causing mediastinal shift
Failure to respond to standard respiratory infection treatments
references: DICER1-related pleuropulmonary blastoma: clinical and molecular features. J Pediatr Hematol Oncol. 2020.
